name: The Slaughtered Lamb
summary: In Stormwind, The Slaughtered Lamb gives gnome warlocks a place to seek training. With King Magni Bronzebeard watching dark practitioners in Ironforge, mentors send their students to human warlocks for instruction.

sections.title: Exile and Scrutiny
sections.body: Before Gnomeregan fell, aspiring warlocks in Khaz Modan studied with tinker-mages and demonic scholars inside the techno-city. The disaster scattered those institutions and drove the gnomes into exile. Surviving practitioners crowded into Ironforge's underground caverns, watched by King Magni Bronzebeard and the dwarven guard. They cannot openly practice demonic arts or perform dangerous rituals there, so senior instructors such as Lago Blackwrench send students away.

sections.title: The Mage Quarter's Secret Cellar
sections.body: Gnome students sent south from Ironforge seek instruction at the Slaughtered Lamb, a tavern in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. Twisting stone passages and stairs lead from its taproom to a hidden sanctum where human warlocks gather. Gakin the Darkbinder oversees the covert gathering. Its space and dark paraphernalia let instructors teach novices to summon and bind minor demons without drawing the immediate anger of the city marshals.

sections.title: Growing Strain in the Shadows
sections.body: Stormwind's coven welcomes capable hands, but the arrival of refugee novices brings friction. Human mentors already risk discovery by the city's paladins and authorities. Gakin and his colleagues find their hidden sanctuary more crowded as practitioners arrive from Khaz Modan. The steady stream from the dwarven mountain could expose their discreet operation, yet neither the gnomes nor the human warlocks have an easier choice.

faq.q: Why can't gnome warlocks train in Ironforge?
faq.answer: King Magni Bronzebeard watches warlocks in Ironforge closely. Since Gnomeregan fell, the displaced practitioners have no private academy, and summoning demons inside the dwarven mountain risks discovery.

faq.q: Where were Khaz Modan warlocks trained before?
faq.answer: Before Gnomeregan fell, warlocks in Khaz Modan trained with tinker-mages and demonic scholars in the techno-city. The disaster scattered those institutions and sent survivors into exile.

Gakin the Darkbinder is a human warlock who oversees the hidden sanctum beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind. He teaches apprentices to summon and bind demons, including gnome novices sent from Ironforge.
The Slaughtered Lamb is a tavern in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. Its cellar hides a gathering place for warlocks, out of sight of the city authorities.

faq.q: Why is Gakin frustrated with the newcomers?
faq.answer: Gakin fears the arrival of many refugee gnomes will draw attention to Stormwind's hidden coven. Space and teachers are limited, and too much warlock activity could expose them to the authorities.
Lago Blackwrench is a gnome warlock trainer who lives in Ironforge's dark alleys. He sends promising novices to Stormwind to continue their training.

angles.text: For young Alliance warlocks, this journey is an essential rite of passage into the hidden network that connects practitioners across racial lines.
In exile, gnomes crowd into Ironforge and rely on human hospitality after losing their academies in Gnomeregan.
Ironforge's authorities watch demonic practice closely, leaving dwarf warlocks in the shadows and sending their students elsewhere.
